title: Hiring Committee Scorecard and Conversion Playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a working template for the cross-functional hiring committee to use when evaluating candidates (full-time, contract-to-perm conversion, and internal transfers) and to standardize post-offer onboarding steps. It combines a calibrated scorecard, quick calibration notes for interviewers, and a practical conversion checklist for contractors moving to permanent roles.

Context / why this exists:
- Interview outcomes have drifted by team; we need consistent rubrics to reduce bias and make decisions defensible.
- We want a repeatable contract->perm process that ties performance signals to a tailored interview-lite loop instead of full re-hiring.
- Committee members are often pulled from Eng, Product, and People Ops; this doc keeps everyone aligned on what the scores mean and next steps.

Quick instructions for committee lead:
- Distribute completed scorecards within 48 hours of final loop.
- Run a 30-minute calibration call when a hire is borderline (combined score between 60–70%).
- For conversion cases, collect at least 12 weeks of performance notes before initiating conversion review.

SCORECARD (single-page canonical format)
- Scoring scale: 1 (insufficient) — 5 (exceptional). No halves.
- Weights are suggested defaults; teams can adjust by exception with People Ops sign-off.

Criteria and weights (default):
- Technical competency (code, systems): weight 35%
- Problem solving & design: weight 25%
- Product sense & scope alignment: weight 10%
- Collaboration & communication: weight 15%
- Ownership & operational maturity: weight 10%
- Culture / values fit & DEI considerations: weight 5%

How to compute the composite score (example):
- For each criterion, map the 1–5 score to a percentage (score/5). Multiply by criterion weight. Sum to get total % (0–100).
- Decision bands (recommended):
  - >= 85%: Strong yes (fast-track offer)
  - 75–84%: Yes (standard offer)
  - 65–74%: Borderline — require calibration review
  - 55–64%: Hold — consider senior interview or assignment review
  - < 55%: No

Rubric guidance (short prompts for interviewers):
- Technical competency (35%): look for clarity, tradeoffs, and correctness. Ask candidate to explain prior system they built. Evaluate depth: breadth ok for senior ICs, depth for individual contributors.
- Problem solving (25%): prioritize approach, hypothesizing, testability, and failure modes. Note whether candidate decomposes problems and iterates.
- Product sense (10%): assess ability to tie technical tradeoffs to user outcomes; look for pragmatic tradeoffs and measuring impact.
- Collaboration (15%): evidence of cross-functional work, code review behavior, feedback receptivity, and succinct status updates.
- Ownership (10%): signals include identifying gaps, following through on incident postmortems, and proposal ownership.
- Culture/DEI (5%): look for inclusive language, respect for diverse viewpoints, and explicit examples of mentorship or advocacy.

Calibration checklist (for the 30-minute call)
- Each interviewer presents their top 2 supporting facts for their scores (1–2 minutes each).
- Call facilitator asks clarifying questions only; avoid re-evaluation on trunk issues.
- Compile a short decision rationale and next steps. Document in hiring ticket.

Interview roles (recommended):
- Hiring manager (HM): decision owner; completes manager rubric and final hire proposal.
- Tech lead / system architect: deep technical assessment.
- Peer IC: culture and day-to-day collaboration.
- Product or PM: product/impact assessment (optional for infra-only roles).
- People Ops: process owner; ensures scorecard completed and extends offer.

Contractor -> Permanent conversion playbook (practical steps)
- Preconditions (minimum signals):
  - 12+ weeks on contract OR 3+ delivered features/modules with code reviews.
  - No unresolved performance incidents; any incidents have documented improvement plans.
  - Manager recommends conversion and provides written examples of impact.
- Lightweight conversion interview matrix (avoid full loop unless risk flagged):
  - 1-hour manager interview (ownership + roadmap fit)
  - 1-hour technical deep-dive with tech lead OR present a recent design doc (prefer doc review to whiteboard)
  - Optional peer chat (30m) focusing on collaboration and cross-team handoffs
- Score thresholds for automatic conversion vs. full loop:
  - If averaged conversion score >= 80% and no compliance flags -> auto-approve to offer stage.
  - 65–79% -> conversion calibration with hiring manager + People Ops; may require one additional interview.
  - < 65% -> recommend full hiring loop (or decline).
- Timeline target: begin conversion review 3 weeks before contract end; complete decision 2 weeks before end date to allow offer negotiation.

Onboarding checklist (first 90 days, condensed)
- Prestart (People Ops + IT): hardware ordered, access requested (1Password, internal SSO, repo access), manager onboarding plan shared.
- Day 1: team intro, buddy assigned, repo walkthrough, first small ticket assigned (env setup verification).
- Week 1: complete security & compliance training, shadow on-call rotation readme, pair on first bug fix.
- Week 2–4: deliver first small feature or fix; 1:1 weekly with manager; first feedback check at end of week 4.
- Month 2: ramp to medium-impact tasks, present a 30-minute walkthrough of work to team, join product planning.
- Month 3: demonstrate ownership of a module, full performance review checkpoint, confirm long-term goals and mentorship pairing.

Manager onboarding responsibilities (quick):
- Create an individualized 30/60/90 plan in the hiring ticket before the start.
- Assign a buddy (peer) and document initial pairing schedule.
- Schedule 1:1 cadence and set initial success metrics.

DEI and bias-mitigation notes (practical):
- Use the rubric prompts to anchor feedback to concrete evidence (quote candidate, link to PR/commit, cite design doc).
- Avoid relying on cultural fit alone; if used, document specific behaviors.
- Prefer asynchronous score submission before calibration calls to reduce conformity bias.

Unresolved / discussion items (work-in-progress):
- Should we add a formal coding assignment for senior infra hires? Trade-offs: signal vs. hiring speed.
- Conversion timeline for contractors on 1099 vs. vendor SOWs needs legal review.

Appendix: sample interview questions (mix, keep short)
- Technical: "Describe a recent production incident you owned. What happened, what did you change, and how did you measure success?"
- Design: "Design a multi-tenant KV cache for short-lived sessions. What are the major tradeoffs?"
- Problem solving: "We have a spike in tail latency at 99.9th percentile — how would you approach diagnosing and mitigating it?"
- Collaboration: "Tell me about a time you changed someone’s mind through a technical argument. What evidence did you present?"

Notes to self / action items for next revision:
- Add example filled scorecard PDF for engineering manager hires.
- Coordinate with Legal on conversion language for global contractors.
- Surface anonymized conversion metrics to leadership quarterly.

Document history / versioning:
- v0.1 (2025-11-04) initial draft by Aisha
- v0.2 (2025-12-08) added conversion thresholds and onboarding checklist (Rina)
- v0.3 (2026-01-12) minor wording edits, added calibration flow (Marcus)

End of document.
